edges.notes: cgroups (v2) are Linux kernel resource controllers for CPU, memory, I/O, and related accounting/delegation per kernel documentation.
Container stacks commonly compose cgroups with namespaces; cgroups are resource control, not namespace views.
Docker on Linux uses cgroups for container resource limits per common deployment understanding.
Kubernetes kubelet and runtimes rely on cgroups for pod/QoS resource boundaries on Linux nodes.
containerd configures cgroups when managing Linux containers.
runc applies cgroup paths when starting OCI runtime bundles on Linux.
Podman uses cgroups for Linux container resource scopes.
CRI-O configures cgroups for Kubernetes workloads on Linux.
systemd organizes services and scopes using the cgroup hierarchy on Linux.
cgroups limit resources; capabilities gate privilege bits — often composed in container hardening.
cgroups scope host resource limits for processes; KVM guests are a different abstraction from cgroup-scoped containers.
